correctness.rationale: The precise uncovered-cell identity separates never-used row-column intersections from selected isolated incidence edges. Every legal edge with two already-used endpoints must join different forest components, because it must destroy an isolated edge. Therefore any legal sequence yields a forest. If a spanning-tree sequence existed, the first moment one bipartition side is exhausted would leave b>=1 unused vertices on the other side. Subsequent legal moves each irreversibly destroy an isolated-edge component. If the prefix has c nontrivial components, s<=c isolated ones, completion requires b+c-1 moves, so b+c-1<=s<=c. Thus b=1 and all components at first exhaustion are edges of a matching, forcing q=p+1. Explicit sequences attain p+q-2 on all p<=q, and p+q-1 when q=p+1. The known duality supplies the skew-zero-forcing corollary. Finite checks verify 22 small boards but do not replace this proof. The implementation directly uses open adjacency and exhaustively reproduces the claimed optimum on 22 small boards and checks the structural lemma on six legal-prefix families.

value.rationale: The Grundy total domination of Cartesian graph products is a motivated published research topic; the exact formula resolves the canonical two-clique product and gives a sharp exceptional dimension regime. The incidence-forest lemma is an explanatory structural mechanism, and the formula simultaneously determines the skew zero-forcing number on an infinite symmetric graph family. It is not a generic substitution or a numerically insignificant optimization without mathematical structure.
